init - dependency validation. every one of these must SIGNAL, not return quietly
init rejects a non-dictionary deps
init rejects an empty deps - log and timer are required
init rejects deps with log but no timer
init rejects a non-dict log value
init rejects a log dict missing the error key
init rejects a non-dict timer value
init rejects a timer whose addjob is not a variant dict
init rejects a timer addjob exposing no custom variant
deletejobs must be rejected HERE, because teardown cannot detect it missing: a dict-valued dep
returns a null-shaped DICT for an absent key, which turns teardown's @[...;ids;handler] from
protected-apply into three-argument AMEND - it upserts the ids into a throwaway dict, discards
the result and logs nothing, so the jobs survive and teardown still reports them removed
init rejects a timer dict with no deletejobs - a silent teardown failure otherwise
init rejects a NON-CALLABLE deletejobs - presence alone is not enough, it lands in the same silent amend as a missing key
disabletimeout was renamed to suspendtimeoutonroll. rejected rather than ignored: the only
callers who set it explicitly set it to 0b to turn the suspend OFF, and silently dropping that
override would flip exactly those callers back to suspend-enabled
init rejects the renamed disabletimeout key instead of silently ignoring it
init rejects a parvaluesrc that is neither log nor tab
init rejects a non-function upd
upd must accept every BINARY function, not just a lambda. a bare 100h=type rejected TorQ's own
default (insert, 102h) and the upsert rdb.md recommends (104h). both restore the default config
init accepts insert as upd - a 102h primitive, and TorQ's shipped default
init accepts upsert as upd - 104h and the documented way to get upsert semantics
init rejects a non-dict savedownmanipulation
init rejects a zero resubscribeperiod - it would run the check every timer cycle
init rejects a negative resubscribeperiod
init rejects an uncastable resubscribeperiod, naming the config key rather than throwing from di.timer
config COERCION. every one of these was accepted before and threw a bare 'type much later:
`boolean$"true" is 1111b, a four-element vector that init stored happily and that only
failed at the FIRST end of day, from inside savetable, naming no config key at all
init rejects an empty tickerplanttypes - it resolves to `, which di.servers matches against EVERY connected process
init rejects a string boolean rather than storing a four-element vector
init rejects a symbol boolean
init rejects a non-temporal timeoutlead - it is subtracted from the roll inside start, AFTER the subscription is live
init rejects a non-date pardefault - it fills the partition list a gateway routes on
init rejects an uncastable tppollms, naming the key rather than throwing from di.servers
init accepts a minute as timeoutlead - a timestamp minus a minute is still a timestamp
init - observable effects. "init did not throw" proves nothing: it passes under a
projection-returning wrong arity too, which is how a two-arg init fails silently
init published upd, endofday, reload and endofperiod at root
